_meta.title: Pro Git (Scott Chacon, Ben Straub)
_meta.pgen: Pro Git EN, ed. 2.1.450 (2026-05-25), 501 PDF pages
_meta.pgbr: Pro Git PT-BR, ed. 2.1.47 (2024-10-28), 500 PDF pages, partial translation
_meta.page_convention: PDF page; printed EN = PDF - 6; printed PT-BR = PDF - 5
_meta.note: Topic index for git_lookup.py. Pages checked by tests/verify_citations.py.

vcs-tipos.name: Types of version control (local, centralized, distributed)
vcs-tipos.summary: Compares local VCS (e.g. RCS), centralized (CVS, Subversion, Perforce: single point of failure) and distributed (full clones as backups; multiple remotes).
mechanisms: Every clone is a full backup of the history
Centralized: if the server is down, nobody can collaborate
gaps: Does not cover monorepos or trunk-based development

snapshots-tres-estados.name: Snapshots, integrity and the three states
snapshots-tres-estados.summary: Git stores snapshots (not differences); almost everything is local; everything is checksummed (40-hex SHA-1); states are modified, staged, committed; working tree, staging area (index), .git directory.
mechanisms: An unchanged file becomes a link to the identical stored copy
Git almost only adds data: what is easily lost is what was never committed
risks: Work that was never committed is probably lost (PGEN p.55)
dated: SHA-1 as the hash; only a passing note says Git is moving to SHA256 (PGEN p.226); PGBR does not even have that [DATED]
gaps: Does not teach how to create SHA-256 repositories (object-format does not appear)

config-inicial.name: Installation and initial configuration (git config)
config-inicial.summary: Three config levels (system, global, local), identity, editor, init.defaultBranch (Git >= 2.28), --show-origin, help (git help, -h).
mechanisms: Repeated key: the last value read wins
git config --list --show-origin
risks: A badly configured editor on Windows can end the operation prematurely (PGEN p.29)
dated: Installation steps and the versions cited (e.g. 2.8.0) are of their time [DATED]
gaps: PGBR does not have the section 'Your default branch name'

init-clone.name: Getting a repository (init, clone)
init-clone.summary: git init creates .git; git clone copies every version of every file and checks out the latest; the 2nd argument picks the directory.
mechanisms: Protocols cited: https, git://, SSH
dated: git:// is discouraged by the book itself in Ch. 4 (PGEN p.115) [DATED in practice]
gaps: Does not cover --depth or partial clone

gravar-alteracoes.name: Recording changes (status, add, commit, rm, mv, .gitignore)
gravar-alteracoes.summary: The status/add/diff/commit cycle; git add is used to track, stage and mark a conflict as resolved; diff compares working tree x index, --staged compares index x last commit; .gitignore with globs; rm needs -f if the file is modified/staged; rm --cached removes it from tracking.
mechanisms: git add stores the content as of the moment of the add
commit -a only picks up files that are already tracked
risks: commit -a can include unwanted changes (PGEN p.44)
git rm -f discards unrecorded data (p.44)
dated: Status messages have the format of their time [DATED]
gaps: Does not teach a global gitignore or .git/info/exclude (refers to the man page)

log-historico.name: History (git log and filters)
log-historico.summary: log -p, --stat, --pretty (format is stable across versions), --graph, date/author/grep filters, -S, path after --, --no-merges.
mechanisms: Several --author/--grep options combine as 'any'; --all-match requires all the --grep patterns
gaps: Does not show --follow; the ready-made log --oneline --graph --all appears only in Branches (PGEN p.74-75)

desfazer-basico.name: Undoing things (amend, unstage, discard local changes)
desfazer-basico.summary: commit --amend redoes the last commit; reset HEAD <file> (or restore --staged, Git >= 2.23) unstages; checkout -- <file> (or restore) discards local changes with NO way back.
mechanisms: amend replaces the commit (new SHA-1)
reset without --hard does not touch the working directory
risks: checkout -- / restore discard with no way back (PGEN p.54, 56)
Do not amend a commit that was already pushed (p.53)
dated: The book shows reset/checkout first and restore only afterwards; current teaching uses restore/switch [DATED]
gaps: Does not cover revert here (only in Appendix C and in merge), nor stash in detail in this section

remotos.name: Working with remotes (remote, fetch, pull, push)
remotos.summary: remote -v/add/show/rename/remove; fetch does NOT merge; pull = fetch + merge; push is rejected if someone pushed first; pull.rebase defines the behavior (warning since Git 2.27).
mechanisms: Renaming a remote renames the remote-tracking branches
remote remove also deletes those branches
risks: A rejected push requires integrating first (PGEN p.59)
dated: The PGBR section 'Pushing to Your Remotes' is in English (PGBR p.52)
gaps: Does not teach pull --rebase beyond the pull.rebase config in this section

tags.name: Tags (lightweight, annotated, sharing, deleting)
tags.summary: An annotated tag (-a) is a full object (tagger, message, signable) and is the recommended kind; a lightweight tag is just a pointer. push does not send tags; --tags sends lightweight and annotated; --follow-tags only annotated; tag -d does not delete on the remote.
mechanisms: Tagging an old commit: git tag -a vX <hash>
checking out a tag gives a detached HEAD
risks: Commits in a detached HEAD become unreachable without a branch (PGEN p.66)

aliases.name: Git aliases
aliases.summary: git config --global alias.<name> '<command>'; the ! prefix runs an external command; examples unstage and last.
dated: The unstage example uses reset HEAD -- [DATED]

branches-basico.name: Branches: pointers, HEAD, create and switch
branches-basico.summary: A branch is a lightweight pointer to a commit; HEAD points to the current branch; checkout moves HEAD and changes the working directory; checkout -b creates and switches; since Git 2.23 git switch / switch -c do the same (PGEN p.76 box).
mechanisms: 3 files produce 5 objects: 3 blobs, 1 tree, 1 commit
git log --oneline --decorate --graph --all
risks: Checkout overwrites the working directory; with conflicting changes Git refuses (PGEN p.74, 78)
dated: Examples use master and checkout [DATED]; PGBR does not mention switch

merge-basico.name: Merge: fast-forward and three-way
merge-basico.summary: Fast-forward only moves the pointer when the commit is directly ahead; diverged history produces a three-way merge with a merge commit (two parents). A merged branch can be deleted with -d.
mechanisms: git merge hotfix -> Fast-forward
'recursive' strategy in the book's message
dated: The recursive strategy is cited; today the default is another one (ort) [DATED, extrapolation]
gaps: Does not include --no-ff, --ff-only or --squash in this section

conflitos-merge.name: Merge conflicts (basic resolution)
conflitos-merge.summary: Git pauses without creating the merge commit; status lists 'both modified'; edit between <<<<<<< ======= >>>>>>>, remove the markers, git add each file and git commit; git mergetool is a graphical alternative.
mechanisms: git add = mark as resolved
risks: Forgetting to remove the markers or to run git add
gaps: merge --abort only appears in Advanced Merging (PGEN p.279-280)

gestao-branches.name: Branch management (list, delete, rename, master -> main)
gestao-branches.summary: branch -v/--merged/--no-merged; -d refuses an unmerged branch and -D forces it (loses work); rename with --move and push with --set-upstream; renaming master requires warning collaborators and adjusting scripts, CI and the host before deleting the old one.
mechanisms: push --set-upstream origin new; push origin --delete old
risks: -D discards unmerged commits (PGEN p.86)
Renaming a branch in use by collaborators is discouraged (p.86)
dated: The book treats the master->main switch as a note [DATED in hosting practice]

workflows-de-branch.name: Branching workflows (long-running, topic branches)
workflows-de-branch.summary: Long-running: only stable code in master and develop/next for testing; topic branches are short-lived and are created, merged and deleted several times a day.
gaps: Does not cover git-flow or trunk-based; no 'git flow' in the text

branches-remotos.name: Remote branches, tracking, push, pull and remote delete
branches-remotos.summary: fetch brings an immovable origin/x (no editable local branch); create tracking with checkout -b / --track / branch -u; explicit push; branch -vv uses data from the last fetch; deleting a remote branch only removes the pointer (data stays until GC).
mechanisms: pull = fetch + merge
risks: credential.helper cache avoids typing the HTTPS password on every push (PGEN p.98)

rebase.name: Rebase: basics, --onto, perils and rebase vs merge
rebase.summary: Rebase replays commits onto another base, producing a linear history with the same final snapshot as a merge. Rule: do not rebase commits that exist outside your repository and on which others may have based work. If someone else's force-push happened: fetch + rebase or pull --rebase.
mechanisms: Rebase abandons commits and creates new, similar ones
patch-id helps detect duplicates, only if the patch is nearly identical
risks: Rebasing published, in-use commits confuses everyone (PGEN p.106-109)
dated: The book only cites --force; --force-with-lease does not appear [DATED]
gaps: Does not include rebase --abort/--continue here (--abort appears in PGEN p.255)

servidor-protocolos.name: Protocols (local, smart/dumb HTTP, SSH, git://)
servidor-protocolos.summary: Local does not protect against accidental damage; Smart HTTP is the most popular; SSH is good on a corporate network; git:// without TLS can allow arbitrary code execution and push over it is open to anyone.
mechanisms: Port 9418 is often blocked
risks: git:// and http:// without encryption (PGEN p.115-116)
dated: git:// is obsolete in practice [DATED]

servidor-ssh-daemon-http.name: Setting up a server (bare, SSH, git-shell, daemon, Smart HTTP)
servidor-ssh-daemon-http.summary: git clone --bare + scp; single git user with authorized_keys and git-shell; git daemon with git-daemon-export-ok; Smart HTTP with git-http-backend (authentication belongs to the web server, use SSL).
mechanisms: ssh-keygen -o with a passphrase; ssh-agent
risks: git-http-backend does not authenticate on its own (PGEN p.124-125)
dated: Examples with systemd/Apache/Ruby of their time [DATED]; PGBR p.107-116 is in English

gitweb-gitlab-hospedagem.name: GitWeb, GitLab and third-party hosting
gitweb-gitlab-hospedagem.summary: GitWeb is simple; GitLab is a full server (more maintenance); in GitLab, 'Destroy' on a user is destructive and 'Block' is preferable.
risks: Destroying removes the user's projects (PGEN p.128)
dated: The GitLab version and hosting services cited are of their time [DATED]

workflows-distribuidos.name: Distributed workflows (centralized, integration-manager, dictator and lieutenants)
workflows-distribuidos.summary: Three models: centralized, integration-manager (fork + pull) and dictator/lieutenants (huge projects).

diretrizes-de-commit.name: Commit guidelines (whitespace, logical commits, message)
diretrizes-de-commit.summary: git diff --check before committing; logical commits (git add --patch); summary of up to ~50 characters, blank line, body of ~72 columns, verb in the imperative; the blank line is critical (rebase gets confused).
risks: Without a blank line after the summary, tools such as rebase get confused (PGEN p.137)
gaps: Does not include Conventional Commits or Signed-off-by as a general format rule

times-e-forks-publicos.name: Contributing: small team, managed team, public fork
times-e-forks-publicos.summary: Small team: fetch+merge and push; managed: one branch per feature and integrators; public fork: push the topic branch to the fork, request-pull, rebase+push -f or a v2 branch, merge --squash for change requests.
risks: push -f after a rebase rewrites the remote branch (PGEN p.152)
gaps: Does not cover --force-with-lease

patches-por-email.name: Patches by email (format-patch, send-email, apply, am)
patches-por-email.summary: format-patch -M; send-email/imap-send; the maintainer uses git apply (all or nothing, does not commit) or git am (preserves author and message; --resolved, --skip, --abort, -3).
risks: Pasting a patch into an email client can break its formatting (PGEN p.154)
dated: PGBR p.149-164 (Maintaining a Project) is in English

manter-projeto-integracao.name: Maintaining a project: integration, review, release (describe, archive, shortlog)
manter-projeto-integracao.summary: Review with git diff master...contrib and git log contrib --not master; integrate by merge, master/develop, master/next/seen/maint, rebase or cherry-pick (new SHA-1); release with tag -s, describe, archive, shortlog.
mechanisms: git describe requires an annotated tag (--tags includes lightweight ones)
risks: The abbreviated SHA from describe may stop being valid (PGEN p.169)

github-conta-fork-pr.name: GitHub: account, fork, pull request, GitHub Flow
github-conta-fork-pr.summary: Fork + topic branch + push to the fork + PR; new commits on the same branch update the PR (without notifying); outdated PR: prefer merging upstream over rebase; if you rebase, do not force-push to an open PR (new branch/PR). The fork never updates itself.
mechanisms: The Merge button always creates a non-ff merge commit
risks: A direct commit to the fork's master gets in the way of syncing (PGEN p.196)
dated: Interfaces, HTTPS password auth and the Sync fork button have changed [DATED]; PGBR translates only up to p.188

github-manter-org-api.name: GitHub: maintaining a project, organizations, notifications, webhooks and API
github-manter-org-api.summary: Collaborators, PRs at refs/pull/N/head (needs an extra refspec), notifications, README/CONTRIBUTING, transferring a project, teams, webhooks (default: push only), API with a token (60 req/h without auth, 5,000 with).
risks: The token only appears once (PGEN p.220)
dated: Webhooks and Services, limits and Basic/token auth [DATED]
gaps: Does not cover GitHub Actions, CODEOWNERS or branch protection

revision-selection.name: Revision selection (short SHA, reflog, ^ and ~, ranges)
revision-selection.summary: Unique short prefix (>=4); rev-parse; reflog and HEAD@{n}; ancestry ^ and ~; ranges A..B, --not, A...B with --left-right.
mechanisms: git log origin/master..HEAD shows what would be pushed
risks: The reflog is local and covers a few months (PGEN p.227)
PowerShell/cmd require escaping @{ and ^ (p.228)
dated: SHA-1 collision demonstrated in 2017; the book cites the migration to SHA256 (p.225-226)

staging-interativo-stash-clean.name: Interactive staging, stash and clean
staging-interativo-stash-clean.summary: add -p for a partial commit; stash saves work (by default it does NOT save untracked/ignored: -u/-a); apply does not restore staged state without --index and does not remove the stash; clean deletes untracked files (use -n before -f).
mechanisms: stash branch <name> for an old stash that conflicts
risks: git clean often has no way back (PGEN p.240)
-x deletes ignored files (p.241)
dated: git stash save is deprecated, use push (PGEN p.236)

assinatura-gpg.name: Signing your work (GPG: tags and commits)
assinatura-gpg.summary: tag -s / tag -v; commit -S and log --show-signature; merge --verify-signatures; commit.gpgsign for the team.
risks: Without standardizing commit.gpgsign the team fails to sign (PGEN p.245)
dated: The book only covers GPG (SSH/S-MIME out) [DATED, extrapolation]
gaps: Does not cover SSH or S/MIME signing

busca.name: Searching (git grep, log -S/-G/-L)
busca.summary: git grep -n [tag] searches any tree; log -S string (when it entered/changed); -G regex; -L :function:file shows a function's history.
gaps: The term 'pickaxe' appears in PGEN but not in PGBR

reescrita-de-historia.name: Rewriting history (amend, rebase -i, squash, split, filter-branch)
reescrita-de-historia.summary: Rewrite only locally and before pushing. amend; rebase -i HEAD~N (pick/edit/squash/drop; deleting a line loses the commit); split via reset HEAD^; filter-branch is the 'nuclear option' and the book recommends git-filter-repo.
mechanisms: Way out: git rebase --abort during, reflog afterwards
risks: Changing a commit rewrites all its descendants (PGEN p.255)
filter-branch changes every SHA-1 when changing an email (p.256-257)
dated: filter-branch: the book itself says it is no longer recommended (PGEN p.255)
gaps: Does not include autosquash/fixup or force-with-lease

reset.name: Reset demystified (three trees, --soft/--mixed/--hard, checkout vs reset)
reset.summary: reset moves the branch HEAD points to (step 1, --soft), then matches the index (--mixed, default) and the working directory (--hard). reset --hard is the only destructive form; with a path, it skips step 1 (= unstage). checkout moves HEAD itself.
mechanisms: Squash: reset --soft HEAD~N + commit
The final table has a 'WD Safe?' column (PGEN p.277)
risks: reset --hard and checkout <commit> <paths> are not safe for the working directory (PGEN p.269, 277)
dated: Does not cover restore/switch or ORIG_HEAD [DATED]
gaps: Does not include reset --keep

merge-avancado.name: Advanced merging (abort, whitespace, manual re-merge, ours/theirs, undo, subtree)
merge-avancado.summary: Clean workdir before merging; merge --abort; -Xignore-space-change; checkout --conflict=diff3; undo a local merge with reset --hard HEAD~, a published one with revert -m 1 (and revert the revert to re-merge); -Xours/-Xtheirs vs -s ours; subtree.
risks: merge --abort may not restore everything when there were uncommitted changes (PGEN p.280)
-s ours ignores the other branch entirely (p.291-292)
dated: recursive vs ort strategy [DATED, extrapolation]

rerere.name: Rerere (reuse recorded resolution)
rerere.summary: rerere.enabled true records preimage/resolution and replays it in future merges/rebases with the same conflict.
gaps: Does not cover rerere forget

blame-bisect.name: Debugging with Git (blame and bisect)
blame-bisect.summary: blame -L, -C annotates lines; bisect: start, bad, good, run <script> (0 = good, non-zero = bad), reset at the end. Use bisect when you do not know where the defect is.
risks: Forgetting bisect reset leaves the repository in the bisect state
gaps: Does not include bisect skip

submodulos.name: Submodules
submodulos.summary: submodule add; clone --recurse-submodules; pull does not update submodules (use submodule update --init --recursive); a submodule sits in a detached HEAD; push the submodule before the superproject (--recurse-submodules=check|on-demand); only worth it if you edit the submodule together with the project.
risks: A forgotten push leaves the superproject pointing to a nonexistent commit (PGEN p.315)
dated: Git < 2.13 behaviors cited [DATED]
gaps: Does not cover submodule deinit

bundle-replace-credenciais.name: Bundle, replace and credential storage
bundle-replace-credenciais.summary: bundle create/verify/list-heads to carry commits without a network; replace grafts history; credential helpers (cache expires in 900 s; store writes in plain text).
risks: credential store keeps the password in plain text and never expires (PGEN p.336, 339)
dated: HTTP password authentication has changed on hosts [DATED]

config-atributos-hooks.name: Customizing: config, attributes, hooks
config-atributos-hooks.summary: autocrlf (true on Windows, input on Linux/macOS); .gitattributes travels with the project but drivers/filters (config) do not; client hooks are not cloned and can be bypassed (--no-verify); real policy lives on the server (pre-receive/update).
mechanisms: update runs per ref; pre-receive runs once
risks: help.autocorrect=1 runs the command automatically (PGEN p.345)
dated: Hook examples in Ruby and P4Merge are of their time [DATED]

politica-imposta.name: Example of Git-enforced policy (message and ACL)
politica-imposta.summary: A server-side update hook validates the message format (regex) and per-path ACLs; client hooks mirror it to warn early.
risks: Client hooks assume the same local and remote user (PGEN p.371)

git-svn.name: Git with Subversion (git svn)
git-svn.summary: git svn clone/dcommit/rebase; keep history linear, rebase instead of merge, dcommit before any Git push; dcommit rewrites commits.
risks: A merge becomes a squash in SVN and loses merge-base information (PGEN p.379-381)
dated: Subversion is little used today [DATED, extrapolation]

mercurial-perforce-migracao.name: Mercurial, Perforce and migrating to Git (fast-import)
mercurial-perforce-migracao.summary: Map authors before migrating; git svn clone --authors-file; hg-fast-export; git-p4 and Git Fusion; custom importer with git fast-import.
risks: Cleaning markers (git-svn-id, git-p4) with filter-branch changes every SHA-1 (PGEN p.411-412)
dated: Git Fusion, Google Code, git-remote-hg: old tools [DATED]
gaps: There is no TFS/TFVC section in the text

internals-objetos.name: Internals: objects (blob, tree, commit, tag) and plumbing
internals-objetos.summary: Git is a content-addressable filesystem; object = header (type, space, size, null) + content, SHA-1, zlib, in objects/xx/yyyy; valid modes 100644, 100755, 120000.
mechanisms: hash-object -w; update-index --add --cacheinfo; write-tree; commit-tree
dated: The whole chapter describes 40-hex SHA-1; SHA-256 repositories are not covered [DATED]
gaps: Does not include object-format or hash migration

internals-refs-tags-head.name: Internals: references (HEAD, tags, remotes) and update-ref
internals-refs-tags-head.summary: Refs are files with a SHA-1 under refs/; use update-ref and symbolic-ref instead of editing files (update-ref feeds the reflog); an annotated tag is an object, a lightweight one is just a ref.
risks: symbolic-ref refuses HEAD outside refs/ (PGEN p.433)

packfiles-gc.name: Packfiles, gc and maintenance
packfiles-gc.summary: A pack stores the most recent version whole and older ones as deltas; automatic gc triggers at ~7,000 loose objects or >50 packs; moves refs to packed-refs.
gaps: Does not include git maintenance or commit-graph

refspec-transferencia.name: Refspec and transfer protocols (dumb/smart)
refspec-transferencia.summary: Default fetch: +refs/heads/*:refs/remotes/origin/* (the + forces a non-fast-forward update); push <src>:<dst>; :topic or --delete deletes on the remote; dumb does not write to the server; smart uses send-pack/receive-pack and fetch-pack/upload-pack.
risks: A refspec cannot be used to fetch from one repo and push to another (PGEN p.440)

recuperacao-de-dados.name: Data recovery and removing large objects
recuperacao-de-dados.summary: Lost commit: git reflog (or log -g) and git branch recover <sha>; without a reflog: git fsck --full and 'dangling commit'. Large file: filter-branch --index-filter 'git rm --ignore-unmatch --cached', clean refs/original and logs, gc and prune --expire now.
risks: Deleting the file in a later commit does NOT remove it from history (PGEN p.449)
prune --expire now deletes permanently (p.452)
dated: filter-branch and manual cleanup with rm -Rf [DATED]
gaps: Does not include reflog expire or gc --prune

variaveis-de-ambiente.name: Git environment variables
variaveis-de-ambiente.summary: Global variables, repository location, pathspecs, commits, network, diff/merge, debugging (GIT_TRACE*) and others.
risks: GIT_SSL_NO_VERIFY turns off certificate verification (PGEN p.454-455)

apendices-ambientes-embutir.name: Appendices A and B (GUIs/IDEs/shells; embedding Git: libgit2, JGit, go-git, Dulwich)
apendices-ambientes-embutir.summary: Autocompletion and prompt in Bash/Zsh/PowerShell (posh-git); GitHub Desktop's Sync button does pull --rebase and push; CLI vs library when embedding.
dated: Versions of IDEs and libraries [DATED]

apendice-c-comandos.name: Appendix C: commands by category and Index
apendice-c-comandos.summary: Lists commands by category citing the book's section (without pages); the EN Index uses printed pages (PDF - 6). git revert is described as a reverse cherry-pick (PGEN p.495).
dated: Appendix C still uses checkout to switch branches and does not list switch/restore/worktree [DATED]
gaps: Does not list git worktree as a documented command
